title: Lakes
source: After the notes' South America and Africa physical maps, with standard UPSC facts added

places.name: Lake Maracaibo
places.significance: South America's largest lake, a tidal bay of the Caribbean over rich oil fields — and Earth's lightning capital, lit by the Catatumbo storms
notes: In Venezuela
The largest lake of South America
Earth's lightning capital: the Catatumbo lightning flashes on most nights of the year

places.name: Lake Titicaca
places.significance: The highest navigable lake in the world, 3,812 m up on the Altiplano, shared by Peru and Bolivia — and drying
notes: Between Peru and Bolivia
The highest navigable lake
Drying

places.name: Lake Poopó
places.significance: A shallow salt lake on the Altiplano, once Bolivia's second largest, that dried up almost completely in 2015
notes: In Bolivia
A dried lake

places.name: Lagoa dos Patos
places.significance: Brazil's largest lagoon, behind a sand bar on the coast of Rio Grande do Sul, with Porto Alegre at its head
notes: The largest lagoon lake of Brazil

places.name: Lake Victoria
places.significance: Africa's largest lake, shared by three countries, which the Equator crosses and the White Nile leaves at Jinja
notes: Shared by Uganda, Kenya and Tanzania
Not a rift valley lake: it fills a shallow basin between the rift's two arms
The largest lake of Africa, and the second largest freshwater lake in the world
Source of the **White Nile**, which leaves it at Jinja, Uganda
The Equator passes through it

places.name: Lake Tanganyika
places.significance: The longest freshwater lake on Earth and the second deepest, filling the western arm of the rift for some 670 km
notes: A rift valley lake
The longest freshwater lake in the world, about 670 km
Shared by the DRC, Burundi, Zambia and Tanzania
The second deepest lake in the world (about 1,470 m), after Baikal

places.name: Lake Malawi
places.significance: The great rift lake at the southern end of East Africa's lakes, shared by three countries
notes: Shared by Malawi, Mozambique and Tanzania
Called Lake Nyasa in Tanzania and Lago Niassa in Mozambique
A rift valley lake, at the rift's southern end
Holds more species of fish than any other lake

places.name: Lake Turkana
places.significance: The world's largest permanent desert lake, an alkaline lake in the rift of northern Kenya
notes: In Kenya — its northern tip in Ethiopia
An example of a rift valley lake
The world's largest permanent desert lake and its largest alkaline lake
The Omo, from Ethiopia, is its main inflow

places.name: Lake Albert
places.significance: A lake of the western rift on the Uganda–Congo border, through which the White Nile flows north
notes: Between Uganda and the DRC
An example of a rift valley lake — the Western (Albertine) Rift
The White Nile passes through it, in from Lake Kyoga and out as the Albert Nile

places.name: Lake Edward
places.significance: A lake of the western rift under the Rwenzori, on the Uganda–Congo border, draining north to its larger neighbour
notes: Between Uganda and the DRC
An example of a rift valley lake — the Western (Albertine) Rift
Drains north, by the Semliki, into Lake Albert

places.name: Lake Chad
places.significance: A shallow lake of the Sahel, shared by four countries, that has lost nine-tenths of its water since the 1960s
notes: Shared by Chad, Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria
Very shallow — a few metres deep
Has shrunk by about 90% since the 1960s, through drought and irrigation

places.name: Lake Volta
places.significance: The world's largest reservoir by area, held back in Ghana by the Akosombo Dam
notes: In Ghana
A man-made lake: the **Akosombo Dam** (1965)
The largest reservoir in the world by surface area

places.name: Lake Kariba
places.significance: The world's largest reservoir by volume, held back on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe
notes: Between Zambia and Zimbabwe
A man-made lake: the Kariba Dam on the **Zambezi** (1959)
The largest man-made lake in the world by volume

places.name: Lake Nasser
places.significance: The reservoir behind the Aswan High Dam, flooding the river's valley across the Egypt–Sudan border
notes: On the **Nile** river
A man-made lake: the **Aswan High Dam** (1970)
Shared by Egypt and Sudan — the Sudanese part is called Lake Nubia

places.name: Lake Tana
places.significance: Ethiopia's largest lake, high on its highlands, out of which the Blue Nile flows
notes: In Ethiopia
Origin of the **Blue Nile**
The largest lake of Ethiopia, about 1,800 m above sea level

places.name: Lake Assal
places.significance: Africa's lowest point, 155 m below sea level in Djibouti, and one of the saltiest lakes on Earth
notes: In Djibouti
155 m below sea level — the lowest point of Africa
One of the saltiest lakes in the world, saltier than the Dead Sea

places.name: Lake Manzala
places.significance: The largest of the delta's coastal lagoons, between Damietta and Port Said
notes: In Egypt
A brackish lagoon on the Nile Delta's north-east edge, beside the Suez Canal's Mediterranean end

places.name: Lake Timsah
places.significance: The small lake halfway along the Suez Canal, on whose shore Ismailia stands
notes: In Egypt, on the Suez Canal
Ismailia stands on its shore

places.name: Great Bitter Lake
places.significance: The salt lake the Suez Canal crosses at its widest, where ships wait and pass one another
notes: In Egypt, on the Suez Canal
Joined to the Little Bitter Lake at its southern end

places.name: Little Bitter Lake
places.significance: The lesser salt lake on the Suez Canal, just south of its larger twin
notes: In Egypt, on the Suez Canal
South of the Great Bitter Lake

places.name: Great Rift Valley
places.significance: A great trench where Africa is splitting apart, running from the Red Sea through Ethiopia and East Africa to Mozambique in two arms
notes: Formed where the African plate is pulling apart — the Nubian and Somali plates
Two arms: the **Eastern** (Gregory) and the **Western** (Albertine)
Its lakes are long and deep: Tanganyika, Malawi, Turkana, Albert, Edward
Lake Victoria lies between the two arms — it is not a rift valley lake
